recognize_zh: 電子顯微鏡下紅血球前驅細胞核內的濃密異染色質（heterochromatin）中散布許多圓形、電子透亮的小洞，呈海綿狀「瑞士起司」外觀，這是 CDA type I 的超微結構特徵。
features: Transmission electron micrograph at high magnification of erythroid precursor nuclear chromatin
Electron-dense heterochromatin masses riddled with numerous round electron-lucent holes of varying size (spongy, 'Swiss cheese' pattern)
Larger lucent inclusion with membrane-like rim within one heterochromatin mass, possibly cytoplasmic invagination
Intervening finely granular euchromatin/nucleoplasm of moderate electron density
Portion of extracellular/cytoplasmic lucent space at lower right
describe_en: Transmission electron micrograph at high magnification of an erythroid precursor nucleus shows irregular, electron-dense heterochromatin masses containing numerous small round electron-lucent vacuole-like spaces, imparting a spongy 'Swiss cheese' appearance. One heterochromatin mass contains a larger lucent inclusion with a membranous rim, suggestive of a cytoplasmic invagination. The nuclear envelope and intercellular chromatin bridges cannot be assessed at this field. Findings are consistent with the characteristic ultrastructure of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.

ddx.vs: CDA II shows peripheral double membranes (ER cisternae parallel to the plasma membrane) and binucleate erythroblasts on light microscopy rather than spongy 'Swiss cheese' heterochromatin.
Megaloblastic erythroblasts show open, finely dispersed chromatin with nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony but lack the lucent holes within dense heterochromatin.

MDS erythroid dysplasia may show nuclear irregularities and ring sideroblasts, but spongy heterochromatin and internuclear chromatin bridges are characteristic of CDA I (CDAN1/CDIN1) rather than acquired dysplasia.
